 Author: BBC News 
 Bangladesh: Garment workers protest for higher minimum wages, hundreds of factories close
 ⓘ 
 Mamunur Rashid, Shutterstock (licensed) 
 Garments workers of Achieve Fashion stage a demonstration in Dhaka, Bangladesh, on February 27, 2023 
 Read more: bbc.com
 Hundreds of garment factories in Bangladesh have been forced to close after workers protested for higher wages, citing rising living costs. The protests turned violent, with clashes between protesters and police, and dozens of arrests. Workers demand a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka ($242; £180), more than double the current standard. The garment industry employs around four million workers in Bangladesh, manufacturing for major global brands such as H&M, Primark, and Uniqlo. The industry generates nearly $40bn annually, accounting for around 10% of Bangladesh's GDP. The government has established a board to review workers' wages, but protests continued on Monday, with around 670 factories suspending operations. Authorities have accused the banned political party Awami League of instigating violence, but no evidence has been provided.
